authors: Thomas KN, Gower DJ, Bell RC, Fujita MK, Schott RK, Streicher JW
title: Eye size and investment in frogs and toads correlate with adult habitat, activity pattern and breeding ecology (Dryad dataset: Thomas_species_traits.csv, 220 species with activity pattern and habitat)
why: Canon compilation for the diel trait in Anura: the dataset's Thomas_species_traits.csv (65,940 bytes) holds the activity pattern of each of 220 species with a source reference, which the main text (read in full) does not. Dryad's file downloads (api/v2/files/432391/download and stash/downloads/file_stream/432391) fail or refuse robots, and the figshare copy of the ESM (ndownloader.figshare.com/files/24584882, 9 MB PDF) redirects to a signed S3 address the fetch tool cannot follow.
get: open access: in a browser open the Dryad page and download Thomas_species_traits.csv, or the Proc B ESM PDF from rs.figshare.com collection 5113670; drop the CSV in the papers folder

title: Color, activity period, and eye structure in four lineages of ants: Pale, nocturnal species have evolved larger eyes and larger facets than their dark, diurnal congeners
why: The article behind the Dryad dataset 10.5061/dryad.nzs7h44v8 already on the canon list; the dataset is SPSS .sav files the fetch tool cannot read, but the article's tables give eye length, facet number, facet diameter, interommatidial angle and visual field span by species for 23 Myrmecocystus, Aphaenogaster, Temnothorax and Veromessor species, with activity period. The PLOS page returned HTTP 429 to the fetch tool.

authors: Banks MS, Sprague WW, Schmoll J, Parnell JAQ, Love GD
title: Why do animal eyes have pupils of different shapes? Supplementary materials PDF (table S1, list of 214 species with pupil shape, eye position and foraging mode)
why: Marked full on the status page, but the file in the papers folder (Banks 2015 Why animal eyes have pupils.pdf, 892 kB) is the 10-page main article only; it cites table S1 and does not contain it. The species-by-species pupil shapes are only in the supplementary PDF, which science.org and PMC do not serve to the fetch tool.
get: open access: on the article page (science.org or PubMed Central) open Supplementary Materials and save the PDF (1500391_SM.pdf) to the papers folder

authors: Sondhi Y, Ellis EA, Bybee SM, Theobald JC, Kawahara AY
title: Light environment drives evolution of color vision genes in butterflies and moths: Supplementary Data 1 (per-species opsin recovery and diel niche, 175 species)
why: The article page (read) has no species table; Table 1 and 2 are statistics. Per-species opsin classes and diel-niche assignments are in Supplementary Data 1 (a spreadsheet) and the Dryad dataset 10.5061/dryad.gmsbcc2kr, neither of which the fetch tool can read. Opsin-inferred, so g at most when logged.
get: open access: Supplementary Data 1 (xlsx) from the nature.com article page, or Dryad 10.5061/dryad.gmsbcc2kr
